newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's 'Gourmet Governor' salutes Kohl's appetite.
newsitem.headline: HK's 'Gourmet Governor' salutes Kohl's appetite.

text.p: Chris Patten, known by some as Hong Kong's 'Gourmet Governor' because of his love of food and expanding waistline, insisted on Thursday that his appetite was as nothing compared to that of German Chancellor Helmut Kohl.
Patten offered up the comment during his final appearance before Hong Kong's Legislative Council prior to the territory's reversion to China at midnight on June 30.
The Governor submitted to mostly friendly questions from the legislators, including one asking him about his fondest food memory since he arrived in the territory back in 1992.

Patten rued the fact that, because of a round of farewell lunches and dinners which began in May, he would not be "lean as a twig" as planned when he departs Hong Kong on the Royal Yacht Britannia in the early hours of July 1.
"I have scaled some peaks in my eating in Hong Kong," he went on to admit to the Legislative Council.

"I will long recall -- as climbers remember ascending the north face of the Eiger -- a meal at one of our most famous restaurants with Chancellor Kohl. All I can say is that he did not let Germany down."
Helmut Kohl, who visited Hong Kong in May, is a mountain of a man who stands over two metres (6.5 feet) in height and weighs more than 280 pounds (127 kg).
